headline: Tonstakers liquid staking protocol: 2 major contract addresses identified, source code and audit documentation located

findings.text: TON blockchain does not use traditional block explorers like Etherscan; discovered primary tsTON token address (EQC98_qAmNEptUtPc7W6xdHh_ZHrBUFpw5Ft_IzNU20QAJav) via TON-native explorer (tonviewer.com, ton.app) and secondary governance token address (EQCkWxfyhAkim3g2DjKQQg8T5P4g-Q1-K_jErGcDJZ4i-vqR) via blockspot.io

Official deployments documentation exists at https://ton-ls-protocol.gitbook.io/ton-liquid-staking-protocol; however, specific per-chain deployment table with all pool/controller/jetton contract addresses not found in single indexed location

CertiK audit report available at https://skynet.certik.com/projects/tonstakers (completed 11/23/2023); audit scope included 28 audited files covering FunC contract logic but explicit per-contract address list not extracted from PDF

GitHub source code located at https://github.com/ton-blockchain/liquid-staking-contract (ton-blockchain org); repository contains contracts/ folder with Pool, Controller, and Jetton implementations but no explicit deployment manifest or hardhat-deploy/broadcast JSON artifacts found in public repo
TON is single-chain protocol (protocol.chains=['TON']); no cross-chain deployments to enumerate
No factory pattern detected for pool enumeration; protocol architecture uses single Pool contract with multiple Controller contracts managed per-validator, not child pool factories
Two addresses discovered via TON-native explorers and third-party aggregators; addresses trace to on-chain explorer pages and audit report metadata but comprehensive upstream sourcing incomplete

rationale.verdict: Discovery walk completed across website (tonstakers.com), documentation (gitbook), source code (github.com/ton-blockchain/liquid-staking-contract), and audit (CertiK). Identified 2 major contract addresses (tsTON token + governance token) with supporting evidence from multiple TON explorers and aggregate platforms. Single-chain protocol (TON) with no multi-chain or factory-based enumeration needed. Pool and Controller contract addresses not definitively listed in public deployment documentation; these may be discoverable via on-chain read APIs or via detailed source code walkthrough of latest broadcast artifacts.

evidence.shows: Official website confirms protocol name, links to gitbook documentation, GitHub org, audit report (CertiK), and bug bounty program
Protocol documentation describing LSt architecture, Pool, Controller, and Jetton roles; no explicit deployed contract address table found
Source code repository with contracts/ folder; README describes Pool, Controller, and Jetton contracts; no deployment manifest artifact found in public repo

CertiK audit report (11/23/2023) with 28 audited files; GitHub monitoring points to ton-blockchain/liquid-staking-contract at commit 35d676f6ac6e35e755ea3c4d7d7cf577627b1cf0; 1 Major issue (Centralization), 4 Medium, 7 Minor, 6 Informational findings resolved
tsTON token contract on TON explorer; identified as jetton_master contract with 'Tonstakers TON' label; active contract with live transaction history
tsTON jetton metadata on TON App; confirms token name, supply (48M tsTON), 107K holders, trading pairs on Ston.fi and DeDust
Secondary reference to governance token contract address EQCkWxfyhAkim3g2DjKQQg8T5P4g-Q1-K_jErGcDJZ4i-vqR (TSTON ticker)
Tonstakers GitHub organization with 3 public repositories (tonstakers-sdk, ton-proxy, DefiLlama-Adapters); no smart contract source code (uses ton-blockchain/liquid-staking-contract instead)

unknowns: D2: Deployed contracts document – Protocol documentation exists at gitbook but does not include comprehensive table of all Pool, Controller, and Jetton wallet contract addresses per deployment

D4: GitHub deployment artifacts – No hardhat-deploy, foundry broadcast, or manual addresses.json file found in public ton-blockchain/liquid-staking-contract repo; deployment artifacts may be stored privately or generated during deployment pipeline

D8: Pool and Controller contract addresses – Primary Pool contract and per-validator Controller contract addresses not yet discovered from public sources; these may require on-chain enumeration or direct API queries

protocol_metadata.about: Tonstakers is the largest liquid staking protocol on TON blockchain, allowing users to stake TON tokens and receive tsTON (liquid staking receipt token) in return. The protocol pools user deposits and lends them to validators through a Pool contract and individual Controller contracts per validator, distributing validation rewards back to stakers. Users maintain liquidity and can utilize tsTON across the broader TON DeFi ecosystem while earning staking rewards.
